summary:
Mission Architect is a browser-based game where players design, launch, and fly a complete space mission. They pick a destination modeled on a real NASA mission (Landsat 9, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, or Europa Clipper). They then build a spacecraft by choosing the bus, science instruments, power source, antenna, radiation shielding, and launch vehicle. Every choice is limited by budget, launch mass (including fuel), power, and data downlink, and a live diagram shows the craft as it takes shape.

A simulated flight then tests the design with launch risk, radiation, and in-flight failures. The debrief explains what limited the mission and compares it to a benchmark design based on the real spacecraft. The game uses published NASA and JPL data for masses, power, instruments, launch contracts, and costs.

Space engineering trade-offs are hard to grasp when they are only described. Letting students make these decisions and see the consequences turns abstract constraints into hands-on learning, with no special equipment required.
details:
Project Details – Mission Architect: Space Mission Design Game

Mission Architect is an interactive educational space mission design game that allows players to experience the challenges involved in planning and executing real space missions. Players can choose between four destinations: Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and Jupiter (Europa). Each destination is inspired by real NASA missions, including Landsat 9, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), and Europa Clipper.

The game allows players to build their own spacecraft by selecting spacecraft components, scientific instruments, power systems, communication antennas, radiation shielding, and launch vehicles. Players must carefully manage four major constraints: budget, launch mass, power consumption, and data transmission. Once the spacecraft is ready, players can launch their mission and experience a simulated journey with possible launch failures, radiation effects, technical anomalies, and other challenges. At the end, the game provides a mission report, science score, performance analysis, and a comparison with a real NASA-inspired mission design.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The main benefit of this project is that it makes space science and spacecraft engineering more interactive and accessible. Instead of simply reading about space missions, players can understand the challenges of designing a spacecraft through practical experimentation. It introduces concepts such as orbital missions, scientific instruments, power generation, communication systems, radiation protection, mass limitations, and mission budgeting.

The intended impact is to encourage students and space enthusiasts to explore STEM subjects, develop problem-solving skills, and gain a better understanding of the engineering decisions behind NASA missions. It also demonstrates how different engineering constraints are interconnected and how a decision in one area can affect the entire mission.

Tools, Programming Languages, and Software:

The project was developed as a web-based application using:

  • HTML5 – For the structure and content of the game.
  • CSS3 – For the user interface, responsive layout, animations, and visual design.
  • JavaScript – For game logic, spacecraft calculations, mission simulations, random events, scoring, and interactive features.
  • SVG – For spacecraft illustrations, animated flight paths, and mission graphics.
  • NASA and JPL resources – For real-world mission information, spacecraft specifications, instrument details, and other reference data.

The game runs directly in a web browser and does not require additional hardware or software installation.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of Mission Architect is the combination of space exploration, spacecraft engineering, and interactive gaming. It transforms complex mission-planning concepts into an engaging simulation where players make their own engineering decisions.

One of its unique features is the use of real NASA mission data alongside clearly identified game estimates. Players can experiment with different spacecraft configurations, discover the consequences of their decisions, and compare their designs against real-mission-inspired benchmarks. The game also includes animated mission launches, random mission events, performance evaluations, and customizable mission patches.

Factors Considered During Development:

Several important factors were considered while developing the project:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using NASA and JPL resources as references for real spacecraft and mission specifications.
  • Resource management: Ensuring that players must balance budget, mass, power, and communication capacity.
  • Mission difficulty: Making destinations progressively challenging based on distance, sunlight availability, and radiation exposure.
  • Reliability and safety: Including spacecraft redundancy, radiation shielding, and possible technical failures in the simulation.
  • Educational value: Making engineering concepts understandable through interactive gameplay.
  • Accessibility: Developing a responsive browser-based game that can be played without installing additional software.

Overall, Mission Architect aims to turn the complexity of space mission planning into an enjoyable learning experience while inspiring the next generation of space explorers, scientists, and engineers.
